positives.probe: consent UI written as HTML markup plus an inline script
positives.evidence: The cookie-choices banner lets the user pick analytics/marketing consent; saveChoices stores the choice in localStorage and PUTs partnerSharing to /api/me/privacy.

optional.why: The only user data sent to the first-party API is the consent choice itself, which UC-03 already covers.

positives.probe: consent flags gate loading tracking SDKs
positives.evidence: choices.analytics gates loading Segment and choices.marketing gates loading the Meta Pixel, so both SDKs only run with the user's consent.

positives.probe: third-party SDKs loaded by script injection, then passed the user id
positives.evidence: Loads Segment and the Meta Pixel from their CDNs and passes user.id to analytics.identify and fbq('init', ..., { external_id }).

positives.probe: Global Privacy Control checked inside a combined condition
positives.evidence: navigator.globalPrivacyControl !== true is part of the condition that gates loading the Meta Pixel.

positives.probe: mirrors the rule's positive example (navigator/window.doNotTrack gates gtag)
positives.evidence: Reads navigator.doNotTrack / window.doNotTrack and only loads and configures Google Analytics when DNT is off.

positives.probe: analytics SDK initialized with a user identifier
positives.evidence: Loads gtag.js from googletagmanager.com and calls gtag('config', ..., { user_id: user.id }).

optional.why: DNT is a user preference signal; the catalog lists UC-03 as related to DNT-07, but the UC-03 text never mentions browser signals.

positives.probe: crash-reporting SDK passed id and email
positives.evidence: Sentry.setUser sends the user's id and email to Sentry, an external crash-reporting service.

negatives.probe: dead read: DNT only becomes a Sentry tag and gates nothing (mirrors the rule's negative example)

positives.probe: early-return DNT guard in front of first-party telemetry
positives.evidence: trackScreen returns early when navigator.doNotTrack === '1', so no screen-view beacon is sent.

positives.probe: behavioral events collected by the first party
positives.evidence: Generates a telemetry session id and beacons the screen name, session id and user id to the app's own /api/telemetry endpoint.

optional.why: DNT is a user preference signal; the catalog lists UC-03 as related to DNT-07.

negatives.probe: sendBeacon (a common third-party tracking primitive) aimed at a relative, first-party URL

positives.probe: device permission checked before sensor collection
positives.evidence: navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'geolocation' }) is checked and recording stops if the state is 'denied'.

positives.probe: GPS sensor read
positives.evidence: navigator.geolocation.watchPosition records latitude, longitude, altitude and timestamp into points.

positives.probe: biometric sensor via Web Bluetooth GATT, using numeric service/characteristic UUIDs
positives.evidence: Connects to a Bluetooth heart-rate strap (service 0x180d, characteristic 0x2a37) and records each bpm reading into pulses.

optional.why: requestDevice shows a browser device chooser, which can be read as a device-level permission request.

positives.probe: session store TTL and cookie maxAge
positives.evidence: RedisStore ttl and cookie.maxAge both expire sessions after 14 days.

positives.probe: HTTPS-only, httpOnly session cookie
positives.evidence: The session cookie is configured with secure: true, httpOnly: true and sameSite: 'lax'.

positives.probe: server-side Sec-GPC header gating ad-conversion sharing
positives.evidence: Reads the Sec-GPC request header and skips the conversion upload when it is '1'.

positives.probe: server-side ad conversion API built with builder objects
positives.evidence: Sends the user id, IP address and User-Agent to Meta's Conversions API via UserData/ServerEvent/EventRequest.

optional.why: GPC is a user preference signal; the catalog lists UC-03 as related to DNT-07.

negatives.probe: server-side dead read: the DNT header is only written to the request log

positives.probe: input validation/escaping plus password hashing (mirrors the rule's bcrypt example)
positives.evidence: express-validator checks and escapes the signup fields and rejects invalid input; the password is stored only as a bcrypt hash.

spans.start: const { email, password, displayName, birthDate } = req.body;

positives.probe: form fields read and stored, plus a login event with IP and UA
positives.evidence: Reads email, display name and birth date from req.body into users, and records the signup IP and User-Agent in login_events.

negatives.probe: plain insert with no TTL or expiry (mirrors the rule's negative example)

optional.why: An authentication guard applied here but implemented elsewhere; the rule's UA-04 example treats @login_required as scoping, not a safeguard.

positives.probe: self-service read of the user's own record
positives.evidence: GET /me returns the users row selected by req.session.userId.

positives.probe: self-service edit of the user's own record
positives.evidence: PATCH /me updates display_name, home_region and phone for WHERE id = req.session.userId.

positives.probe: request-body profile fields persisted
positives.evidence: Reads displayName, homeRegion and phone from req.body and writes them to the users table.

positives.probe: endpoint for setting marketing, sharing and visibility preferences
positives.evidence: PUT /me/privacy lets the user set marketing_opt_in, partner_sharing and profile_visibility.

optional.why: Stores user-supplied data, but the data is only the preference flags UC-03 covers.
An update scoped to the user's own record, but of settings rather than of 'their information'.

positives.probe: 'download my data' export
positives.evidence: GET /me/export zips the requesting user's profile, activities and comments, each queried by their own id.

optional.why: Generates and stores a user-linked credential, which is not personal data in the usual sense.

negatives.probe: crypto.randomBytes is present, but the token is stored in plaintext (crypto-looking trap)

positives.probe: account closure done as anonymization plus deferred erasure, via POST
positives.evidence: POST /me/close blanks the requesting user's email, password hash and phone, and queues erasure of their content.

positives.probe: retention bound expressed as a delayed queue job
positives.evidence: cleanupQueue.add('erase-member-content', ..., { delay: 30 days }) erases the member's content 30 days after closing.

positives.probe: role-based authorization guarding a destructive operation
positives.evidence: requireRole('support') restricts deleting any member's record to support staff.

negatives.probe: admin delete of an arbitrary user id (mirrors the rule's negative example)
static configuration constant (mirrors the rule's negative example)

positives.probe: encryption from raw primitives (createCipheriv aes-256-gcm) under a non-obvious name
positives.evidence: sealNote encrypts activity notes with AES-256-GCM using a random IV and auth tag before they are stored.

positives.probe: raw fetch to an unfamiliar external domain, with a pseudonymous id
positives.evidence: POSTs the user's route polyline, start time and a tm-<userId> reference to ingest.routeshare.example.

negatives.probe: gated by an operator env flag, not a user choice

positives.probe: a per-user score derived and persisted with no request input
positives.evidence: Derives a readiness score from the user's recent distance and heart rate and saves it to users.readiness_score.

negatives.probe: a hand-written formula, not an ML model
a 28-day query window is a filter, not a retention mechanism

positives.probe: uploaded file with location and heart rate persisted
positives.evidence: Parses the uploaded GPX file and stores the route geometry, distance, average heart rate and notes for the user.

optional.why: Call site of sealNote (the encryption is implemented in AV2); also carries the requireAuth guard.
Call site of shareRouteWithPartner (the transmission is implemented in AV4).

positives.probe: user deletes one of their own records
positives.evidence: DELETE /activities/:id removes the activity only when user_id matches the requester.

positives.probe: object-level authorization folded into the SQL WHERE clause
positives.evidence: The AND user_id = $2 ownership condition, with a 404 on no match, stops users from deleting other people's activities.

positives.probe: user-generated content stored
positives.evidence: Reads the comment text from req.body and inserts it with the author's user id.

optional.why: requireAuth guard applied on the route line.

positives.probe: external model output drives an automated action (mirrors the rule's moderation example)
positives.evidence: The comment text goes to OpenAI's moderation model, and a flagged result hides the comment with no human review.

positives.probe: user content sent to an external AI provider
positives.evidence: openai.moderations.create sends the user's comment text to OpenAI.

positives.probe: a user preference controls disclosure to other users, not collection or sharing
positives.evidence: profile_visibility === 'private' makes the endpoint return only id and display name to anyone but the member.

optional.why: The visibility branch doubles as an access-control check on profile data.

negatives.probe: reads an arbitrary member by path id; not scoped to the requester

positives.probe: inbound webhook signature verification
positives.evidence: stripe.webhooks.constructEvent checks the Stripe-Signature against the webhook secret and rejects payloads that fail.

optional.why: The rule's TP-02 negative example notes this kind of internal save 'may still qualify separately under FP-01'.

negatives.probe: a call into an internal module (mirrors the rule's internalOrdersService negative example)

positives.probe: marketing email gated on an opt-in flag (mirrors the rule's positive example)
positives.evidence: The digest returns without sending unless member.marketing_opt_in is set.

positives.probe: email provider SDK passed the address and profile fields
positives.evidence: sgMail.send passes the member's email, name and home region to SendGrid.

positives.probe: email provider SDK passed the address and billing details
positives.evidence: sgMail.send passes the member's email, name and payment amount to SendGrid.

negatives.probe: transactional email sent unconditionally (mirrors the rule's negative example)

positives.probe: scheduled purge of aged records (mirrors the rule's positive example)
positives.evidence: A daily cron job deletes login_events rows older than 90 days.

positives.probe: user data flagged for model training (mirrors the rule's training-data example)
positives.evidence: Stores the user's coach transcript and rating with include_in_training=True.

optional.why: Persists user content; the rule's own example classifies this only as AI-08.

positives.probe: fine-tuning corpus signalled only by 'sft' naming and chat-format JSONL
positives.evidence: Appends user coach transcripts as {'messages': ...} JSONL records to the datasets/coach_sft directory.

positives.probe: per-user data sent to an LLM API for generation
positives.evidence: The member's name, birth date, readiness score and recent activities go into a prompt for client.messages.create.

positives.probe: personal and health data sent to an external AI provider
positives.evidence: The Anthropic API call sends the member's name, birth date and heart-rate history outside the first-party boundary.

optional.why: The generated plan is derived content about the user and is persisted.

only aggregate, non-user-linked data goes to the LLM and Slack

positives.evidence: Terminates TLS (TLSv1.2/1.3 with AEAD ciphers) and sets an HSTS header.

positives.evidence: The trailmark log_format records each client's $remote_addr and $http_user_agent.
